ResStock 2025 Release 1 Measure Documentation: Advanced Air Sealing, Attic Floor Insulation, Duct Sealing, and Drill-and-Fill Wall Insulation Accessing Results This documentation covers the “Advanced Air Sealing, Attic Floor Insulation, Duct Sealing, and Drill-and-Fill Wall Insulation” measure upgrade methodology and briefly discusses key results. All results are available on the ResStock™ Open Energy Data Initiative “End-Use Load Profiles for the U.S. Building Stock” data lake and on the data viewer at resstock.nlr.gov. Measure Summary Measure Title Advanced Air Sealing, Attic Floor Insulation, Duct Sealing, and Drill-and-Fill Wall Insulation Measure This upgrade measure package applies advanced air sealing, attic floor insulation, Definition duct sealing and insulation, and drill-and-fill wall insulation for applicable dwelling units. A dwelling unit may receive none, some, or all four measures, depending on its housing characteristics. Applicability This measure applies to all dwellings with at least one of the following housing characteristics: • Infiltration rate of 6 ACH50 or higher • Unfinished attic & less than R-49 attic floor insulation & in climate zone 1 • Unfinished attic & less than R-60 attic floor insulation & in climate zones 2 through 8 • Duct leakage to outside greater than 6% • Duct insulation less than R-6 • Uninsulated above-grade exterior wood stud walls. With these applicability constraints, 98% of existing dwelling units receive at least one of the measures. Not Applicable This measure does not apply to dwelling units that have none of the following housing characteristics: • Equal or more than 6 ACH50 infiltration rate • Unfinished attic & less than R-49 attic floor insulation & in climate zone 1 • Unfinished attic & less than R-60 attic floor insulation & in climate zones 2 through 8 • More than 6% duct leakage to outside • Less than R-6 duct insulation • Uninsulated above-grade exterior wood stud walls. These constraints exclude 2% of dwelling units from receiving this measure upgrade. The goal of these upgrades is to reduce heat loss in winter and retain cool air longer in summer. Air sealing alone does not eliminate the need for insulation (DOE, 2025). Insulation and air sealing work best together to improve comfort and energy efficiency. Therefore, they are often completed as a package to address complementary aspects of a home’s energy efficiency, and their combined effect is much greater than any single measure alone. Together, these upgrades help to lower energy bills, improve indoor comfort, and enhance indoor air quality year-round. 1.1 Introduction to Technology Air Sealing Air sealing involves identifying and closing large and small gaps, cracks, and penetrations in the home’s primary or secondary pressure boundaries such as around windows, doors, attic hatches, and plumbing or wiring holes (DOE, 2025).
